text_fidelity_a:
iKanzi Beach Blanket, Sandproof Waterproof Beach Mat Outdoor Picnic Blankets for Travel, Camping, Hiking (Orange+Blue) When I read the description of this product I was excited but a bit worried about what kind of quality this would be. I have 3 very rough and tumble grand kids that I have recently been taking to the parks and lakes and was uncertain if it would stand up to their antics. Boy was I surprised!!

As you can see by the product description and the pictures, that the item was quite compact which is great. But don't let the small size of the packaging fool you, the beach mat is HUGE when laid out. It will indeed hold 4-9 people easily.

The fabic is thin making it light weight, but I found it to be very durable as well. Enough that having the kids run over it, even when advised not to, it stood up very well. It is very strong for being so thin and light weight, I have no doubt this is going to hold up fantastically on our next camping trip and beach trip.

The shipping was super fast and it arrived just as we were leaving for the lake to let the kids play on the beach and in the water. I was super stoked that when we were done, the sand and dirt feel right off, NOTHING was tracked in my car. I hate trying to get sand out of my car upolstry and carpets! But one of the best features is that because it is water proof, when we got to the car it was large enough that I could put across my seats and keep my seats dry from the kids' wet clothes. I am very happy I don't have to have that wet/damp smeel permiating my car, especially in the Texas hot sun.

Also, I should mention, unless I missed it I didsn't see where it stated it came with stakes to hold it down against the wind, so I was super excited to see that they were included! Awesome bonus! We didn't need the stakes, but will certain use them in the future on our next camping trip.

I have used this Sunlite Standard Schrader Valve Tube as a replacement tube for the ones I've damaged during hard use. Having it delivered to me saves about an hour of my time that I would have spend driving to/from and waiting for a salesperson to pull the tube. Time gets more valuable as I get older so I appreciate any time that I can use to be more productive. I always make sure that I have a spare tube sitting on the shelf for the next repair in case one gets punctured. text_fidelity_a:
Nautilus R514 Recumbent Exercise Bike (Discontinued) The bike arrived via UPS in a carton that looked as if it had been through an aerial bombardment. At his suggestion, we went over it with the UPS driver and took pictures, but it looked as if the contents had somehow survived unscathed. We were wrong. After assembly (about 45 minutes) my son sat on the bike and THE PEDALS WERE FROZEN IN PLACE.

We called the Nautilus help line. After a short wait (perhaps 2 minute), we connected with a helpful worker who transferred us to the right tech department (and gave us a direct number in case we were disconnected (YES!). In short order the problem was diagnosed and a tool shipped to us. It arrived 4 days later. We were then able to complete the repair (the coupling controlling the resistance force had slipped from its mounting during shipping).

SINCE THEN - All is well. The bike is very quiet, easily adjusted to different riders and has all the bells and whistles that could be asked for in a sub $1000 machine. It was a bit more expensive than some of its competition, but not withstanding our problem, the build quality is first rate. Welding, hardware, electronics assembly, and even upholstery all seem well done, often with fasteners that seem larger than might be thought neccessary.

Our problem was a consequence of mishandling. Was it the fault of the manufacturer, Amazon or UPS? I don't think we can tell. But it makes us much less likely to order large box items from Amazon.
text_fidelity_b: Nautilus R514 Recumbent Exercise Bike (Discontinued)

I got this as a way to get myself walking regularly.  Understand that I live in Texas and until this week when we had 24 hours of rain that resulted in 10 inches of rain - nearly as much as we were down for 3 months...before that we had I believe 67 days in a row of 100+ degree days with even the night temps barely dipping below 90.  Skinny people may be okay walking in that heat, but not a fat person trying to lose weight!  So, for me, I have been walking slow and in short "bursts" to get acclimated and able to move up in speed and time.  T had been wanting an easy treadmill to store as I live in a small house - a mobile home which is the early version of a tiny house, before tiny homes were a "thing."  Anyway, I have this in my bedroom stashed behind a chair next to my bed.  It is easy to pull out and step on to begin my walk.  At the moment, I am walking about 15 minutes at a time.  My goal is to get to 1 hour and then I can begin walking faster to get some cardio involved with the walk.  I have also incorporated yoga so that I am working on muscle strength as well.  This treadmill is helping, but I was afraid, when I got it, that it wouldn't work well for me because I was a bit too heavy for it.  That's why I would ask that the people who make this should look into making it sturdier for those of us who are trying to improve our heath by using a treadmill.  Make it handle 300 or maybe up to 350 pounds would make it helpful for those who want to take charge of their weight loss at home.

text_fidelity_a:
Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Hitch Mount Rack , Silver/Black (522RR) Believe the reviews that say this is terrific! I had some concerns about the small receiver shaft wobbling in my 2-inch hitch, but Allen Sports has really figured it out with their "wobble bolt." My rig is tight and vibration free.

From the pictures it looked like the plates on the hitch were plastic shims, but they are well-designed (removable) plates screwed to the main shaft. And their design -- again -- contributes to the rigidity of the frame when mounted.

I mounted this rack in less than 10 minutes, threw on the bikes and drove 700+ miles without any issues whatsoever. Bikes arrived without a scratch and as secure as they were when I left the driveway.

There are only three factors of this hitch that I'll point out:
1) It is an inch or two higher than it needs to be, so the bikes are in the rear window of my SUV. (This could be an adjustable setting of the rack if Allen Sports (or I, I suppose) would drill a couple of different holes in the upper piece of the rack.)
2) It does trigger the proximity sensors in my rear bumper. So I had to dig through the owner's manual to figure out how to disable that.

As others have mentioned, the frame of the bike will bang on the vertical section of the rack if not attended to. I wrapped a thin sheet of foam rubber around the upright and secured it with some black duct tape I had handy. You can't even see the pad, and it cushions the frame of the first bike when tied down with a bungee cord.

My favorite feature of this rack is the tilting mechanism. It makes it trivially easy to move the bikes out of the way for access through the tailgate.

Overall, one of my best Amazon purchases this year. I've compared Yakima and Thule racks at 3-5+ times the price and can't find anything in them that is superior to this one.
text_fidelity_b: Allen Sports Deluxe 2-Bike Hitch Mount Rack , Silver/Black (522RR)

text_fidelity_a:
Uflex C5X08 C5 Engine Control Cables for Mercury & Mercruiser, 8' So the image on this ad is obviously not the product for sale. 6+ months after verifying this with the seller, the wrong image is still in place. Seller is great though. Ordered 2 of these in April '21 and finally got around to fitting them in October '21 only to find out one of the cables was a 20' cable. Even though I was well out of return window, TX Parts LLC stood behind their sale and sent me the correct part and a label to return the wrong one.
As for the part itself, it is the correct part for my 1986 Mercury 9.9hp outboard, but the round plastic cylinders that lock into place inside the engine are slightly off in their shape. The small cylinders in the new cables are the same overall length as the originals, but the new ones have flat ends and the original parts have a slight dome end to them. Due to this, the new cables will not lock into place. However, a quick sanding of the edges of the cylinder to make it a dome shape and it fits perfectly. text_fidelity_a: Ontario Knife Rat-1 Knife, 5in. Closed I quite love this blade.. I bought the coated version to leave in my car as a utility knife, but very quickly it found its way into my pockets.. There are a few issues with this knife:  I had to immediately borrow a star key tool to change the clip over to the tang.. I don't really care if it carries tip up or down (comes tip down) but the clip is a bit large on this knife and just in the way, particularly for a knife with such great ergonomics.  The coating on the blade is also not the best.. Also mine had a few little imperfections throughout the blade- just a little pitting here and there.  Still, pretty quickly this knife has made it into my rotation.  The main reason is its ease of use.  The washers have worn in quite well and though it was a bit stiff out of the box, within a week, it opens like butter.. I've typically always favored old-school slipjoint pocket knives over locking knives for carry, but i really see the ease of one-hand use in this design.  The weight and size of the blade also really add to the inertia upon opening so it's just a really satisfying knife to flip open.. Other people might balk at the grips- I thought they felt a little cheap in the hand when I first inspected the knife, but they've turned out to be pretty solid, textured just enough to prevent slippage if they got wet.  Is it the best knife for the money?  I don't know- I bought mine for around 15 bucks and at that price wasn't expecting much:  Just a decent linerlock with a soft enough blade to easily keep sharp- something for the car-  but its size, ease of use and just good solid blade design make for a really practical tool knife which i carry more and more.
text_fidelity_b: Ontario Knife Rat-1 Knife, 5in. Closed

text_fidelity_a: KGM Vector Quintuple Refined Butane Gas Fuel Refill I needed a clean sorce of butane gas to refill a micro torch. Let me put it like this. I found it! No cloging of fuel delivery lines what so ever! I would like to see Vector make it available in a larger size. I do find it quite expensive but because refillable butaine comes in a variety of sizes and grades it dificult at best to determine what you are actually paying for. Like when you buy a gallon of gas, we can esily compare pricing even on premium grade. Someone needs to resolve this issue to assure customers are not getting ripped off. I'm not saying I was, I'm saying I have no clue and I feel it is way over priced compared to other brands that I have previously bought. Then again I need one thats refined to work in mini torches and this one does the trick. So its a matter of, you get what you pay for. Vectors super refined butane costs more in my opinion but one has to pay for quality. Were not talking a huge difference in price. To me a few bucks more for a quality product that I can be sure will work properly is well worth it. Concider the alternative, you clog up, mess up and possibly destroy your torch with an infirior product is not going to make you very happy. I got this advice direct from the torch manufacturer and I quote "I cant recomend a specific brand but make sure you use high quality butane refill to avoid fuel delivery system clogging". Thats enough for me. I cant find any other butain refil thats refined 5 times. Quintuple? Thats 5 right? I don't know but it seems to be alot of refineing going on here. The more it is refined the cleaner and purer it is. It is also nice to know that I am buying butane in a can and not butane combind with who knows what else but what ever it is it can ruin your torch. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is, I am a tuff cookie to earn 5 stars from me it has to be perfect. I want a larger size can and I want to see some priceing so I can be an informed consumer and understand what I am paying for. Yup I am picky I know. Like I said, good stuff and I will be ordering more! I hope ya'll have found this helpfull.
text_fidelity_b: KGM Vector Quintuple Refined Butane Gas Fuel Refill

Etekcity LED Camping Lantern for Emergency Light Hurricane Supplies, Lanterns for Survival Kits Power Outages, Battery Powered Operated Lanterns Lamp, Camping Gear Accessories, 4 Pack I got this product in the mail and was very impressed. It is a great lantern for the price. And it uses 3 AA batteries instead of D cell batteries.

Build - It is built very well. It is a sturdy construction that can withstand normal use and some heavier use. it is not indestructible but based on the price I would not expect that.

Convenience - This lantern is a good size. And when you store it away you just push the lid down to turn it off and it compacts to a smaller size to take up less space.

Low power - It uses 3 AA batteries and will stay lit for 12 hours. Once the batteries get to a certain point the lights dim to conserve what little power is left in the batteries. I do wish that the LED lights were is sections so once a section is pushed in so far that section turns off so it saves batteries and is less bright than you need it. but that would make the price go up.

Handles - I like that the handles will fold down when not in use and you can use the handles to hang the lantern however you need to hang it. The handles are metal and are somewhat sturdy. I think the handle could be better. Make it a hard plastic and build it into the lid.

All in all this is a great little lantern and I love that is runs off AA batteries. I will get a lot of use out of it.
text_fidelity_b: Etekcity LED Camping Lantern for Emergency Light Hurricane Supplies, Lanterns for Survival Kits Power Outages, Battery Powered Operated Lanterns Lamp, Camping Gear Accessories, 4 Pack

TiGr Mini+ Titanium Bike Locks. This Bicycle U Lock with Mounting Clip is Heavy Duty, Lightweight & High Security. Features Disc-Style U-Locks with 2 Keys (4"/102mm Wide, 8"/203mm Long) I commute by bike, and I have to carry my bike up and down a flight of stairs 5 days a week. My bike is an e-bike that weighs 50 lbs without any gear attached. After adding a rack, trunk bag, lights, etc., it's probably up to 60 lbs. The bike is fairly expensive, and I work on a university campus, so I need a lock I can rely on. I originally purchased the [[ASIN:B005VMO49U Abus Bordo GRANIT X Plus 6500/85cm (33.46 in) black - Folding lock, Bike lock, Security level 15]] because of it's high security rating. But it's SO HEAVY!!! It's almost 5 lbs., which means it adds 10% to the weight of my already very heavy bike. Hauling my bike PLUS that lock up and down the stairs was just too much.

Now I have this lock. I love this lock! It's so light! It barely adds any weight to bike. It's also easy to lock. I like that I can remove the barrel, position the lock, and then replace and lock the barrel without the key. The security rating on this isn't as high as the ABUS, but I see so few of these in the wild that I don't think your average bike thieves are prepared to break this lock. At least I hope not.

As an added bonus, my e-bike has a cage mount on it's battery, and that's where I've attached this lock. So when I remove the battery to charge it, this lock serves as a very welcome handle for the rather heavy battery. :)

As far as I know, no one's tried to break my lock yet, so I can't say for certain how secure it is. But it has a good rating, it feels secure, and it's light and easy to use. So I'm happy.
text_fidelity_b: TiGr Mini+ Titanium Bike Locks. This Bicycle U Lock with Mounting Clip is Heavy Duty, Lightweight & High Security. Features Disc-Style U-Locks with 2 Keys (4"/102mm Wide, 8"/203mm Long)

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large I've had my Fitbit Flex for about a week. At first, I was fairly impressed when I actually counted my steps and compared it to the Fitbit calculations. However, it can be very quirky and inaccurate under certain circumstances. I have mine on my right wrist, and I am right-handed, so I made sure to set it to the "Dominant" wrist setting. But, to get truly accurate readings, your arm really needs to be at your side. If I'm carrying things around the house, I don't get an accurate count. If I'm walking through the store, pushing a grocery cart, I don't get an accurate count. It seriously under counts my steps. I'd like to send it back and exchange it for the Fitbit One, which I have since heard is more accurate. However, I didn't realize that Amazon only takes returns on unopened items, and otherwise charges a restocking fee. And, I'm not sure this is defective. I think it's just not accurate. Should have bought this from a Brick & Mortar store.

Edited 4/1/2014...Ok, I've been using my Fitbit for a few more days. Today I was out for several hours and my step count was still really low as, described previously, I don't walk with my hands down at my side. I'm usually busy doing other things. I had contacted Fitbit regarding the problem, but the only thing they could say was that it compared to other wrist-trackers on the market....which isn't saying a lot. I'd really like to return or exchange this thing, but can't. When I got home this afternoon, and saw that my step count was again very low, I decided to try taking the Flex unit out of the wrist band and I put it in my pocket. So far, that seems to give me a better step count. Not sure how it will work that way with the other functions. But, frankly, after using the Flex for over a week, I'm not confident in the accuracy of the other functions and will probably never use them. There is an Omron brand clip-on that gets rave reviews. Check that one out before you decide to buy the Flex.

Edited 4/3/2014...I pursued my issues with Fitbit customer service, and this is what they said: " Flex will count your steps when you're walking with your arms stationary, as we do want to give you credit for this activity. This includes walking while pushing a stroller or shopping cart, or holding on to a treadmill. However, because your hands are not moving, your step count may be a bit lower during this activity."

So, they have finally admitted the count is not accurate unless your arms are down at your side. I do dispute the fact that it is a "bit lower." My steps are hardly being counted at all, unless my arm is down at my side. So, for this reason, I have now lowered my rating to two stars. I did contact Amazon customer service and explained what was going on. They are allowing me to return it, without restocking charges, because it is not working as intended. THANKS AMAZON!!!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large

Schrade SCHF36 Frontier 10.4in Stainless Steel Full Tang Fixed Blade Knife with 5in Drop Point and TPE Handle for Outdoor Survival, Camping and Bushcraft I have zero business affiliation with amazon or Shrade. I just like to help people make a decision on purchasing affordable gear. Many times I have bought less expensive gear and was sorry I did. However this won’t be the case with Schrade. If you are just getting into camping/bushcraft start with this knife. I bought my knives directly from the Schrade website (shut down now) about 2-3 years ago. I have 3 of their knives Sch37, Sch57, and Schf52; and was only out of about $60 for all 3. They are great knives for a beginner. Yes, they have some issues. But they may not bother everyone.

The Bad: The basic handles are not the most comfortable over long periods of use. Later, get the micarta scales the basic scales are not comfortable when chopping or don’t chop.

The chimpping on top is a bit aggressive when not wearing gloves and doing percussive tasks.

The protective coating scratches and stains but; it can be removed and cleaned if you have the time. I like to keep my things looking brand new. I may remove the coating at some point.

The sheath is not the greatest but at least you don’t have to buy one.

The good: it comes with a sheath, a sharpening stone, and a fire steel. You don’t get that with $500 knives.

It can accomplish every task a $500 knife can.

You can sell the knife/knives for what you paid; if you want to upgrade.

You can keep them to loan out or for a buddy to use.

Best of all is the price. You get to test out your skills for less than $30 bucks with this knife.
text_fidelity_b: Schrade SCHF36 Frontier 10.4in Stainless Steel Full Tang Fixed Blade Knife with 5in Drop Point and TPE Handle for Outdoor Survival, Camping and Bushcraft

text_fidelity_a:
Myklops Rear View Mirror On the whole, I'm happy with my purchase and find it very useful when I'm riding. I've got a folding bike, which I love but limits my choice of mirrors. I tried different ones that attach to glasses or helmets, but I could never find one that quite fit; besides, I always worried they would drop off the moment I hit a bump. I figured the Myklops was my best option.

As others have noted, objects in this review are a heck of a lot closer than they appear. However, I've gotten used to this and find the mirror very helpful for spotting cars, trucks, and other larger vehicles in traffic. For spotting other bikes, skateboarders, and standing scooter riders (scooterists?), it's not as helpful. Being smaller, they're usually on me well before I pick them up in the mirror. Luckily, that's usually not a problem. With motorcycles and mopeds/scooters, it's a mixed bag. The bigger they are, they easier they are to pick out in the mirror. Usually it's the noise of their engines that I notice first, then I know to look for them in the mirror. So this mirror is helpful, but not as much as I'd like.

Sturdiness is hard to speak to without lots of time going by, but I've been using this regularly for over six weeks, tossing it into bags when I'm not riding with it, and it's holding up. I find the cover a little fiddly to close, but it does latch into place with a little patience. The biggest challenge was remembering to push the arms back into the base before taking by backpack off once I'd gotten to where I was going, but that's pilot error on my part. I don't yank at the arms or twist them hard, but neither am I super delicate with them. They feel the same as they did out of the package, so I'm hopeful that they'll last a while.

As for stability, I find the mirror to be very stable once I've extended the arms and positioned it how I like. The band sometimes shifts around my wrist as I ride, but I don't think this is a fault of the product. I usually wear long-sleeved shirts, the material of which is often a bit loose, so I need to be more careful about smoothing that down and not letting it bunch before fastening the strap. When I'm wearing shorter sleeves with tighter fitting sun gloves, the band stays in place. Also, I'm very pleased that the velcro on the band is on the gentle side. By that I mean that it doesn't have large teeth of the sort that often damage my clothes. Despite being careful, I sometimes catch my clothing on it, but so far (touch wood) it hasn't caused any pilling or tearing of the fabric ... and these are fairly delicate materials I'm talking about, so that's a major bonus.

I think it's impossible to make a perfect mirror that fits all my riding needs. But this comes pretty darn close. Funnily enough, as I sat down to write this review, I noticed that there's currently a nice little discount for it, no doubt for Black Friday/Cyber Monday/or other seasonal sales holiday here. I paid full price for mine, but I'm okay with that. At full price, I feel like I got my money's worth, and I would definitely buy this again.
text_fidelity_b: Myklops Rear View Mirror

text_fidelity_a: Rocket stove with handle, A portable wood burning camping stove with a fire poker & tongs. wood burning Rocket stove with Large Fuel Chamber Best for outdoor cooking. tent heater & emergency. I have messed around with DIY rocket stoves with some success - my best was in using concrete blocks.  They work, but who wants to carry around 4 or 6 concrete blocks in their car?  It's not awful, but this rocket stove is lighter weight and works pretty much the same way.  One really good deal with this rocket stove is that it has the slide on grate pieces so that a pot/pan can be put on top to cook food, boil water for coffee or whatever.  It also gives off heat so when you are out camping, you can sit near it while cooking and not worry about the wind changing direction and open flames burning you as might happen with a regular fire.  Not just that, but with this rocket stove, you can gather small twigs that wouldn't keep a regular fire going and in a rocket stove, they burn well.  I think if I were to make any changes to this design, I'd change the legs.  I'm no engineer, but I think a folding mechanism could be used so the legs are permanently attached, but fold down so the rocket stove is as small as it is now (without the legs being removed and possibly lost).  The same with the slide on grate pieces.  Again, I am not an engineer so it may be that hinges that close to heat might be an issue, but if the grate pieces could be slightly curved so they rest against the stove pipe section, then the same would be accomplished with them as the legs.  The less you have to keep track of, the less that can be lost, right?  Of course if you have a "rocket rucksack" to store it in and maybe the inside is that heat mat stuff so you could place it under the stove while using it and then fold it up to store the stove in it...hey, just some suggestions to the manufacturer for the next iteration!  As far as this rocket stove goes, I am very pleased with it's performance.
text_fidelity_b: Rocket stove with handle, A portable wood burning camping stove with a fire poker & tongs. wood burning Rocket stove with Large Fuel Chamber Best for outdoor cooking. tent heater & emergency.

text_fidelity_a:
POLAR H10 Heart Rate Monitor, Bluetooth HRM Chest Strap - iPhone & Android Compatible, Black I've a had a polar HR strap in the past and really liked it. This one is nice as well, it is comfortable and appears to give accurate heart rate readings. one thing is that I got the M-XL size and wish I had the small instead. this one still fits a little loose even all the way the tightest it can be. For reference, I wear a 34 band in my bra (sometimes a 32, I'm sort of in between). Wearing this under the bra band holds it up okay, I've worn it for 2 workouts now and haven't had an issue of it falling down, though I have yet to wear it on a run. I wanted this to work with my Concept 2 rowing machine, but so far I have been unable to get the concept 2 to recognize the polar H10. I have had no problem getting the Wahoo Run and the Wahoo X HRMs to connect with my rowing machine, but for some reason no go on this. I've tried 3x and no luck. However, it does connect with my iPhone just fine and I use the FitDigits app to do the tracking (so I can't speak for a Polar app, as I dont use that).

I attached a screenshot of the heart rate tracking. You can see in the middle where I was switching from the NordicTrack (it does not have any electronics, it's an old school NordicTrack skier) to the rowing machine where my heart rate is down, that I spent about 4 minutes fiddling with trying to get the Concept 2 to recognize the Polar and no go. Kind of a bummer, but not a deal killer to me since I have the app.

I still rely on my Wahoo HRM, but it's been a little flaky lately with the heart rate, I think. I use it for runs and bike rides with my old Garmin 310XT watch since that only has an ANT+ connection. Can't use this bluetooth polar with it. (would love any recommendations for an upgrade for my Garmin 310xt to use for running and biking if anyone has a comment on that!)

So overall, I'd say this is a good HRM - if I do get the rower to finally recognize it, I'll update this review.

*****UPDATE***** June 4, 2017:

Thanks to a tip from Geekrevival, I updated the firmware on my Concept2 rowing machine and now it recognizes the Polar H10! yippee! To be clear, if you have the Concept2 rower you need to have the PM5 performance monitor for it to recognize Bluetooth Smart (BLE), otherwise only an ANT+ connection will work. You can easily tell if you have the PM5 as it is right in the upper right corner of the monitor.

I updated the review to a 5-star because there's nothing I see as a flaw or downside on this Polar H10 heart rate monitor.

Now I just need to convince hubby that I need that new Garmin fenix5 GPS watch which uses Bluetooth Smart (and ANT+). :)
text_fidelity_b: POLAR H10 Heart Rate Monitor, Bluetooth HRM Chest Strap - iPhone & Android Compatible, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) This is a great concept. I never purchased the original fitbit because I wanted a heart rate feature. The problem is the heart rate accuracy during CrossFit/HIIT/strenuous-type exercises. The accuracy is spot on during the day, and seems equally accurate during mundane exercises (running, cycling, rowing machine, etc). The inaccuracies show up during virtually any other style of workout. I have corresponded a substantial amount with fitbit, and they say they are working on improving the algorithms. Who knows if they can figure it out.

While I would like to see it being accurate during my workouts, one of my biggest complaints regarding it's accuracy is the "lag time". Meaning, how long after the activity is over does the fitbit take to begin showing an accurate heart rate. I would think a few seconds is reasonable. Well, it takes 30-45 minutes!! I don't understand why, and fitbit was unable/unwilling to tell me why. I have tried wearing it on both wrists, at varying tightnesses and locations on my wrists, and taking it off for a few minutes and then putting it back on. Nothing helps, it still takes 30+ minutes for it to be accurate again.

So how is it inaccurate? It reads REALLY low. It will typically read 50-60 bpm low during and immediately after an intense workout. My actual heart rate is 160-180 and the fitbit will say 95-110.

I gave it 3 stars because everything else about it is great and useful. So if your workouts are walking/running/cycling or other similar types of activites, it will work great for you. For those doing similar exercises as me, it will only be useful for monitoring heart rate throughout the day and while sleeping. I decided that was useful enough to keep it, though it was close. It becomes a personal decision as to the value of it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

1-3 BIKEHAND Bike Bicycle Floor Type Parking Rack Stand - for Mountain MTB & Road Bikes Indoor Outdoor Garage Storage The stand holds the bike upright and so it will not fall sideways.
Because it grips the front wheel so that it cannot turn right or left.

Nor slip backwards out.
And as you can see in the picture the bottom of the stand makes the bile roll back uphill,
and so gravity holds the bike from rolling backwards.

I do not agree with those who say this should work to hold a bike in the back of a pickup.
The bike could bounce out (overcome gravity) and roll backwards out.

In the garage, you will want a cover over the bike and stand to keep dust and dirt
out of the parts that have grease (the chain for instance).

Indoors you need a long pad (like an exercise pad to keep the dirty tires off the carpet.

Another (better for cleanliness) is a 'work stand' because these hold the bike in the air
and only the stand touches the floor (like a Park brand work stand). But these take about
15 seconds to load and unload the bike instead of 2 seconds like this Bikehand parking rack.
And work stands are much more expensive.
But a work stand hold bike so that you can do mechanical work on it, thus saving paying
hundreds to a bike shop for repacking bearings and such that you can do yourself with
a work stand and some specialized bike tools.

There are lots of other ways to go too, holders that mount to the wall or ceiling,
some have hoist ropes to raise and lower.

This stand is a very sensible and cheap solution, just keep in mind when the
bike is in a garage, then it needs a cover (cloth or plastic). Amazon sells
lots of these covers, they cost less than this stand.
text_fidelity_b: 1-3 BIKEHAND Bike Bicycle Floor Type Parking Rack Stand - for Mountain MTB & Road Bikes Indoor Outdoor Garage Storage

Probably my favorite feature is its simplicity. A lot of people want bells and whistles and wouldn't be happy with this, but it's perfect for this not-athletic person. I'll never get up to the faster speeds, but to be honest, it shakes enough under my weight when I attempt a light jog, that I'd be just a little leery of pushing it any more. Otherwise it feels sturdy though, and I'm not afraid of it breaking or anything.

As others have said, a second set of hands really helps when putting it together initially. It's not hard, just awkward. My mom helped me by just holding things still or handing me parts. It maybe took a half hour from start to finish, and I was taking my time. Getting it exactly where I wanted in my small room was the hardest part. Folding it up is easy - it's heavy, but I'd be scared to use anything lighter!

This is my first treadmill, and I think it's perfect for a casual user. I doubt I'll ever be an avid walker/jogger, but this at least gives me ample opportunities for exercise when I need it, without worrying about time of day or weather.

NZT1 M2 Night Vision Monocular I was a little bit skeptical of this thing when I first started looking at it. They advertise it more as a camer accessory than an actual night vision monocular. I decided to buy mine used as I am new to the night vision thing.

I love this thing! So here it is

Pros:
Solid
Functions as expected for generation 1
Comes with an illuminator
Great light gathering without the illuminator
Lens caps
Commonly used batteries cr123 for it and 9v for the unit
Carrying strap
Rubber eye piece
Huge objective lens around 80mm
Adjustable diopter
Adjustable objective
Long range 200yards on a crescent moon night without illuminator

Con's:
Heavy!!
Lots of focusing of the objective lens
Awkward to hold/the illuminator gets in the way a little
No actual on/off switch-just a button to push to charge the intensifier last about 2mins a push
Battery is awkward to put in

Overall this thing is awesome, especially for a beginner!

I paid less for it because it wasn't brand new, but it is well worth the money. I highly recommend this to new night vision users.

If you have been using other gens, this probably isn't for you.

text_fidelity_a:
Epson PULSENSE PS-100 Heart Rate Monitor with Activity Tracking for iOS - Black M/L The Pulsense seems like a pretty cool heart rate monitor in theory, but unfortunately falls a bit short in actual use. It’s easy to put on the wrist, and the M/L size fit me fine. It’s not too obtrusive, and while not sexy, it’s not horrendous looking either.

Setting up the device and syncing it with my iPhone was pretty easy. And it was comfortable enough to wear all day at first. But the lights and vibrations that notify you on your heart rate (what target zone you’re in) got annoying real fast – thankfully they can be deactivated. And I found myself reflexively looking at the unit whenever I wanted to know the time – but there’s no clock on it, doh! I really wish there was a digital readout that could toggle between clock and heart rate.

When it works, I like the Pulsense a lot. But I found a lot of lapses in data collection, specifically with the heart rate. At times, it shows that I was at a resting heart rate, when I know that I was actually very active. Not really sure why this happens, and I haven’t been able to pin point it to any specific activity, location, etc.

While there is a lot of potential with the Pulsense (especially not having to wear a chest strap), I’m not so sure that it’s ready for prime time. I’m excited to see how the next version will be improved.
text_fidelity_b: Epson PULSENSE PS-100 Heart Rate Monitor with Activity Tracking for iOS - Black M/L

text_fidelity_a:
Aosom Youth Scooter, Teens Kick Scooter, Adjustable Handlebar Ride On Toy for 5+ w/Front and Rear Dual Brakes Inflatable Wheels UPDATE: On the 3rd time riding this scooter, the brakes malfunctioned and one whole brake pad actually ripped off. This very well could have been our fault because there are not detailed instructions on the brakes. I contacted the company to try to get a replacement brake piece. I think there was a language barrier and we couldn’t get the customer service rep to understand the problem even when photos were sent. To my total surprise, they ended up sending us a brand new scooter. I misunderstood and thought they were only sending the one part so this was quite the surprise. I’m very happy about this because now we have a whole scooters worth of replacement parts.

Original Review:
Overall this looks like a nice scooter and should do my son for a while. The first thing we did was remove the tacky stickers from it and it immediately looked more expensive. The instructions that came with it are the absolute worst instructions I have ever seen. They do not include a list of parts, a list of tools needed or actually describe the steps. We are handy people, I assemble things all the time with very little effort. I've assembled many bicycles and scooters in the past. The video was useless as to how to install the handlebars, it only covered brakes and had only cheesy music, no actual verbal instructions so you had to kind of guess what the guy was doing. The guy in the video was using tools that were not included nor listed as needed for the job. The videographer also did not zoom in when he should have to show the small details. It took us 10 times longer than it should have to get this thing put together because the directions suck so bad. It's too bad because I would have given this 5 stars if there were even halfway decent instructions. It is a nice scooter especially for the price but be prepared to get extremely frustrated with the assembly.
text_fidelity_b: Aosom Youth Scooter, Teens Kick Scooter, Adjustable Handlebar Ride On Toy for 5+ w/Front and Rear Dual Brakes Inflatable Wheels

text_fidelity_a:
Rapidfire Chimney Starter Whether you are firing up your grill, starting a fire in a pit, or any activity that uses charcoal... this is the easiest and bet way to light your coal.

You can use this with lump charcoal or briquettes. All you need to do is light some newspaper in the bottom and let it sit for a couple minutes... before you know it you will see a vortex of flame and some red hot charcoal.

I use this when I grill as well as when I visit state and national parks. There's nothing quite like being able to cook your lunch in the picnic area without all of the waiting for your coals to get hot.

Pros:
- Lights all coal quickly and evenly.
- Lightweight
- Cools quickly
- Feels solid and the handle stays cool

Cons:
- The second handle really isn't necessary. It can get in the way... luckily it's easy to remove.
- Doesn't hold enough coal to completely fill the kettle... maybe I use too much when I sear steaks but if you ask me... 2 of these is a better deal.

Overall this is one of those "must haves" for anyone who uses charcoal to grill.
text_fidelity_b: Rapidfire Chimney Starter

Survival Personal Water Filter (Blue Travel Strap) I firmly believe in being prepared, no matter where you live. Growing up, I watched a tornado tear through our front yard, had streets away from us evacuated, and seen our streets flood. You never know what nature has in store, and I am not waiting until it's too late to try and find clean water for my family. A couple of inches of water outside can cause you to have no access to clean water, and there is only so much space to store up water bottles. I have read articles about personal water filters and I'm so excited to have one now. I will be keeping it in my purse so I always have a way to have and share clean water. Easy to use, just like drinking through a straw. I think everyone should have one, especially with climate change causing a lot of unexpected flooding and crazy weather. Water is the one thing you can't live without. Even food is not so important.
Makes sure the water you drink won't give you parasites, bacteria and infections. Use a filter.

I was a bit disappointed that my first Kleen Kanteen was a single wall. It is a great container and quality product. Just the single container doesn't keep liquids as cold as the double wall ones.
Still, it works great. I've designated this one to the fridge, where I always keep a ready to drink container with cold water.

What I really like about this one is how the water sweats and beads on the outside. Call me weird, but I like that. Reminds me of a the stainless steel water pitchers you see at nice conference lunches. The water beading outside of it somehow makes that look so refreshing. Makes me want to drink more water.

This one all silver with no logo markings on the sides. I will be putting on some decals and keeping this in my fridge at work. I'll just fill it up from cold water dispenser we have and keep it to my side in my fridge. Yup, that is the plan. Will be better than having an open cup on my desk or fridge that I may spill.

It probably does rate a 5 star for a single wall container. I'm just used to double wall ones. This is my first Kleen Kanteen and I was excited when ordering it that I didn't pay attention to full description.

Not the first time I've done that and probably not the last. Still a good experience!
text_fidelity_b: Klean Kanteen Wide Mouth Single Wall Stainless Steel Water Bottle (w/Wide Loop Cap) - 40oz - Brushed Stainless
